raw.description: The application fetches URLs provided by the user without validation, leading to potential Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF).
raw.exploit: An attacker could provide a URL pointing to an internal service, potentially accessing sensitive data or causing unwanted actions.

raw.description: The application displays user-provided data (URL preview) without proper sanitization, which could lead to Cross-Site Scripting (XSS).
raw.exploit: An attacker could manipulate the URL to include a script in the title or description, which would execute in the context of the user's browser.

raw.description: The application does not enforce HTTPS, which could lead to sensitive data being transmitted over an insecure connection.
raw.exploit: An attacker could intercept HTTP traffic to capture sensitive information such as session tokens or user data.

raw.description: The application relies on environment variables for database connection strings without ensuring they are securely stored or accessed.
raw.exploit: An attacker with access to the environment could extract the database connection string and gain unauthorized access to the database.

raw.description: The application lacks Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) protection for the /api/preview endpoint.
raw.exploit: An attacker could trick a user into making unwanted requests to the application, potentially causing actions on behalf of the user.
